questions.question: Fundamental Duties were added under which part of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IVA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution of India by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• They are enshrined under **Part IVA** of the Constitution of India, specifically in **Article 51A**.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were introduced based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**, which was constituted in 1976.
 
• Initially, there were 10 Fundamental Duties, but the **86th Amendment Act, 2002**, added one more duty, making a total of 11 Fundamental Duties.
 
• The Fundamental Duties apply to all Indian citizens and are aimed at promoting a sense of responsibility and commitment towards the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part IV**

 
 
• Part IV of the Indian Constitution deals with the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**.
 
• The DPSPs are non-justiciable guidelines provided to the state to ensure socio-economic welfare and justice.
 
• Examples include provisions for securing a living wage, equitable distribution of resources, and promotion of educational and economic interests of weaker sections.
 
• They are included in Articles 36 to 51.
 
 
 
• **Part VIA**
 
 
• Part VIA does not exist in the Indian Constitution.
 
• This option might have been presented as a distractor in the question.
 
 
 
• **Part VI**
 
 
• Part VI of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions related to the **States in India**.
 
• It includes Articles 152 to 237, which specify the structure, powers, and functions of the state governments.
 
• It encompasses the Governor, State Legislature, High Courts, and subordinate courts.
 
• Part VI does not deal with Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the government's fiscal policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To ensure maximum employment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fiscal policy refers to the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy. The primary goal is to achieve economic stability and growth.
 
• One of the main objectives of fiscal policy is to ensure maximum employment by stimulating economic activities and creating job opportunities.
 
• Governments often increase spending on infrastructure, health, education, and other sectors to boost employment levels.
 
• Fiscal policy also includes tax cuts or incentives for businesses to encourage investment and hiring.
 
• By ensuring maximum employment, fiscal policy contributes to reducing income inequality and improving the standard of living.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Main Tools of fiscal policy:**

 
 
• Government Spending: Direct spending on infrastructure, defense, education, etc., or transfer payments.
 
• Taxation: Adjusting income tax, corporate tax, sales tax, etc., to influence spending and investment.
 
• Public Debt Management: Borrowing and managing government debt levels. 
 
 
 
• **Types of Fiscal Policy**
 
 
• Expansionary: Used during recessions; involves increased spending or tax cuts to boost demand, output, and employment.
 
• Contractionary (Deflationary): Used to fight inflation; involves reduced spending or higher taxes to decrease demand.

questions.question: Which five-year plan focused on food, work and productivity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seventh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Seventh Five-Year Plan** of India was operational from **1985 to 1990** and focused on improving food production, generating employment opportunities, and enhancing productivity.
 
• Its main objective was to achieve a **self-sustained economy**, emphasizing modernization of agriculture and rural development.
 
• The plan aimed to achieve a target growth rate of **5% annual GDP growth**, but it surpassed expectations by achieving approximately 6% growth.
 
• It introduced **programs like Jawahar Rozgar Yojana**, focusing on employment generation in rural areas.
 
• This plan also laid special focus on **social justice and reducing poverty** by improving the living standards of the poor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985)**

 
 
• The focus was on poverty reduction, employment generation, and technological self-reliance.
 
• This plan emphasized the removal of poverty through the **Integrated Rural Development Program (IRDP)**.
 
• It also aimed to achieve economic growth through industrial modernization and agricultural development.
 
• The concept of **Minimum Needs Program** was introduced to improve living standards by providing essential facilities like education, healthcare, and drinking water.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1978)**
 
 
• The main focus was on **poverty alleviation** and achieving self-reliance in agricultural and industrial production.
 
• It introduced programs like the **Minimum Needs Program** and **Garibi Hatao** (Eradicate Poverty) to address socio-economic inequalities.
 
• Due to political instability, the plan was terminated in 1978, one year before its scheduled completion.
 
 
 
• **Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992-1997)**
 
 
• It focused on **economic liberalization** and structural reforms to integrate the Indian economy with the global market.
 
• The plan aimed to reduce fiscal deficits, encourage privatization, and promote industrial growth.
 
• It highlighted the importance of human resource development through investments in education and healthcare.

questions.question: Animals where the fertilisation of eggs and the development of the baby up to the fetal stage takes place inside the mother's body are known as _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**viviparous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Animals that give birth to live young ones and where fertilization occurs internally are classified as **viviparous animals**.
 
• In viviparous animals, the embryo develops inside the mother’s body, and nourishment is provided through a placenta or other internal structures.
 
• Examples of viviparous animals include most mammals, such as humans, lions, and whales.
 
• Viviparity ensures better protection and survival chances for the offspring as they develop in a controlled internal environment.
 
• Viviparous reproduction is an advanced evolutionary adaptation compared to oviparity (egg-laying), as it increases the likelihood of offspring survival in challenging environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oviparous**

 
 
• Oviparous animals lay eggs, and the development of the embryo occurs outside the mother’s body.
 
• Fertilization can occur either internally (e.g., birds, reptiles) or externally (e.g., fish, amphibians).
 
• Examples include hens, frogs, snakes, and fish.
 
• Oviparity is common in species where external environmental factors provide suitable conditions for egg development.
 
 
 
• **Vertebrates**
 
 
• Vertebrates are animals that possess a backbone or spinal column.
 
• They belong to the phylum Chordata and include classes such as mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fish.
 
• Both oviparous and viviparous animals can be vertebrates.
 
• Examples include humans, snakes, frogs, and sharks.
 
 
 
• **Invertebrates**
 
 
• Invertebrates are animals that lack a backbone or spinal column.
 
• This group includes animals such as insects, arachnids, mollusks, crustaceans, and sponges.
 
• Most invertebrates are oviparous, though there are some exceptions.
 
• Examples include octopuses, spiders, and jellyfish.

questions.question: Who was the British Governor-General during the Revolt of 1857?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Canning**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lord Canning** was the British Governor-General during the Revolt of 1857, also known as the First War of Indian Independence.
 
• He served as Governor-General of India from 1856 to 1858 and later as the first Viceroy of India from 1858 to 1862.
 
• Lord Canning introduced several reforms during his tenure, including the establishment of universities in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras in 1857.
 
• After the revolt, the Government of India Act 1858 was passed, transferring power from the East India Company to the British Crown, marking the end of Company rule in India.
 
• Lord Canning is also known for his policy of conciliation, aimed at pacifying the Indians after the revolt by introducing measures like the Indian Councils Act of 1861.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Dalhousie (1848–1856):**

 
 
• He was the Governor-General of India before Lord Canning and is known for his policy of annexation, called the Doctrine of Lapse.
 
• Important annexations during his tenure include Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur, and Awadh.
 
• He is credited with introducing railways, telegraphs, and postal systems in India, contributing significantly to modernizing the country.
 
 
 
• **Lord Curzon (1899–1905):**
 
 
• He is known for the controversial partition of Bengal in 1905, which led to widespread protests and ultimately the Swadeshi Movement.
 
• Lord Curzon also established the Archaeological Survey of India to protect and preserve India’s historical monuments.
 
 
 
• **Lord Ripon (1880–1884):**
 
 
• He is remembered for his liberal reforms, including the introduction of local self-government in India, making him popular among Indians.
 
• Lord Ripon also repealed the Vernacular Press Act of 1878 and introduced the Ilbert Bill, which sought to allow Indian judges to try British offenders.

questions.question: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023, which of the following states has the largest percentage of poor people?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023** (MPI) is based on indicators including health, education, and standard of living.
 
• According to the 2023 MPI, **Jharkhand has the largest percentage of poor people** in India, accounting for approximately 29.4% of its population being multidimensionally poor.
 
• The MPI measures poverty using 12 indicators across three dimensions: **health, education, and living standards**.
 
• Jharkhand has historically faced challenges such as low literacy rates, poor healthcare facilities, and lack of infrastructure development, contributing to its higher poverty index.
 
• The state government is actively working to address poverty through schemes like **Jharkhand State Livelihood Promotion Society (JSLPS)** and initiatives in rural development, skill training, and health improvement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Meghalaya**

 
 
• While Meghalaya has a significant percentage of poverty, it has performed better in certain dimensions of MPI such as health and education compared to Jharkhand.
 
• Meghalaya has undertaken initiatives to improve literacy rates and healthcare accessibility, including programs like the **Meghalaya Health Insurance Scheme**.
 
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh**
 
 
• Uttar Pradesh has a large population base, and poverty alleviation remains a challenge despite numerous development schemes.
 
• The state has implemented programs like **Mission Shakti** and **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana** to improve living standards and women's empowerment.
 
• While poverty levels are high, they are lower than Jharkhand's in terms of multidimensional poverty.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**
 
 
• Andhra Pradesh has shown significant improvement in poverty reduction due to developmental initiatives such as **Navaratnalu**, focusing on healthcare, housing, and education.
 
• The state has a relatively better MPI ranking compared to Jharkhand due to its focused approach towards improving infrastructure and social welfare.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Multidimensional Poverty Index**

 
 
• The MPI is prepared by **NITI Aayog** in collaboration with the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• The index is based on the findings of the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5)**.
 
• It is a tool to assess poverty beyond income, focusing on multiple indicators like nutrition, child mortality, school attendance, sanitation, and access to drinking water.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, which state of the following states has the highest population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census 2011, Bihar has a total population of approximately **104 million**, making it one of the most densely populated states in India.
 
• Bihar accounts for about **8.6% of India's total population**, with a population density of 1,106 persons per square kilometer.
 
• The state's population growth rate between 2001 and 2011 was nearly **25.42%**, which is among the highest in the country.
 
• Bihar's population is predominantly rural, with **88.71% of its population living in rural areas** and only 11.29% residing in urban regions.
 
• Bihar has a **sex ratio of 918 females per 1000 males**, which is slightly below the national average of 940 as per Census 2011.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **West Bengal:**

 
 
• West Bengal had a population of approximately **91.3 million** as per Census 2011, making it the fourth most populous state in India.
 
• It has a population density of **1,028 persons per square kilometer**, which is one of the highest densities in the country.
 
• West Bengal's urbanization rate is higher compared to Bihar, with **31.89% of its population living in urban areas**.
 
• The literacy rate of West Bengal stands at **76.26%**, reflecting better educational attainment compared to some other states.
 
 
 
• **Rajasthan:**
 
 
• Rajasthan had a population of approximately **68.5 million** as per Census 2011, making it the seventh most populous state in India.
 
• It is the largest state in India by area but has a comparatively low population density of **200 persons per square kilometer**.
 
• Rajasthan's population is predominantly rural, with **75.12% of its population living in rural areas**.
 
• The sex ratio of Rajasthan is **928 females per 1000 males**, slightly above Bihar's ratio.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu:**
 
 
• Tamil Nadu had a population of approximately **72.1 million** as per Census 2011, ranking sixth in terms of population among Indian states.
 
• It has a population density of **555 persons per square kilometer**, higher than Rajasthan but significantly lower than Bihar.
 
• Tamil Nadu is among the most urbanized states in India, with **48.45% of its population living in urban areas**.
 
• The literacy rate of Tamil Nadu stands at **80.09%**, showcasing advanced educational progress.

questions.question: In which functional group is the carbonyl carbon attached to the hydrogen atom as well as to the carbon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aldehyde**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An aldehyde is an organic compound in which the carbonyl carbon is bonded directly to a hydrogen atom and an alkyl or aryl group (R group).
 
• The general formula for aldehydes is **R-CHO**, where R represents an alkyl or aryl group.
 
• The carbonyl group (C=O) in aldehydes is highly reactive, making aldehydes important intermediates in organic synthesis.
 
• Aldehydes are commonly found in nature, often as components of essential oils, flavoring agents, and fragrances (e.g., formaldehyde, benzaldehyde).
 
• Some aldehydes, like formaldehyde, are widely used in industrial applications such as resins, plastics, and disinfectants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amides:**

 
 
• Amides are organic compounds containing the functional group **-CONH2**, where the carbonyl group (C=O) is attached to a nitrogen atom (NH2).
 
• They are derived from carboxylic acids by replacing the hydroxyl group (-OH) with an amino group (-NH2).
 
• Amides are important in biological systems, such as in the structure of proteins where peptide bonds are formed between amino acids.
 
• Examples include acetamide (CH3CONH2) and benzamide (C6H5CONH2).
 
 
 
• **Carboxylic Acids:**
 
 
• Carboxylic acids are organic compounds characterized by the presence of a carboxyl group (-COOH).
 
• The carboxyl group contains a carbonyl group (C=O) attached to a hydroxyl group (-OH).
 
• Carboxylic acids are weak acids and are widely found in nature, such as acetic acid (vinegar) and citric acid (citrus fruits).
 
• They are used in the production of polymers, pharmaceuticals, and food additives.
 
 
 
• **Ketones:**
 
 
• Ketones are organic compounds in which the carbonyl group (C=O) is attached to two alkyl or aryl groups.
 
• The general formula for ketones is **R-CO-R'**, where R and R' are alkyl or aryl groups.
 
• Ketones are used in various applications, including solvents (acetone), fragrances, and intermediates in chemical synthesis.
 
• Unlike aldehydes, ketones do not have a hydrogen atom directly attached to the carbonyl group.

questions.question: Who among the following was a member of the High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arjun Ram Meghwal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Arjun Ram Meghwal**, a senior politician and Union Minister, was a part of the High-Level Committee formed to deliberate on the feasibility of Simultaneous Elections in India.
 
• The High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections was constituted in September 2023 to explore the possibilities and challenges of implementing simultaneous elections for Lok Sabha and state assemblies.
 
• The committee was chaired by former President **Ram Nath Kovind**, with notable members such as **Arjun Ram Meghwal** and other eminent personalities.
 
• Arjun Ram Meghwal has extensive experience in parliamentary processes and governance, making him a suitable member of this critical committee.
 
• The committee's objective is to assess the legal, political, economic, and logistical aspects of conducting simultaneous elections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nitin Gadkari**

 
 
• Nitin Gadkari is the Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways and is not a member of the High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections.
 
• He is known for his contributions to infrastructure development, including highway construction and rural road connectivity through programs such as the Bharatmala Pariyojana.
 
 
 
• **Subrahmanyam Jaishankar**
 
 
• Dr. S. Jaishankar is the current Union Minister of External Affairs and was not involved in the High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections.
 
• He is an expert in foreign policy and international relations, contributing significantly to India's diplomatic engagements globally.
 
 
 
• **Jagat Prakash Nadda**
 
 
• Jagat Prakash Nadda is the National President of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and has not been listed as a member of the High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections.
 
• His role primarily revolves around party leadership and organizational strategies for the BJP.
 
 
 
• **Simultaneous Elections**
 
 
• The concept of simultaneous elections refers to holding elections for the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies at the same time.
 
• The idea aims to reduce the costs and administrative burden associated with frequent elections in India.
 
• It requires significant amendments to the Constitution and election laws, along with consensus among political parties.

questions.question: The Bundi Utsav is a popular festival in________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bundi Utsav** is an annual cultural festival celebrated in the Bundi district of Rajasthan.
 
• The festival is organized by the Rajasthan Tourism Department to showcase the rich heritage, culture, and traditions of the state.
 
• It features various activities such as traditional music performances, folk dances, art exhibitions, and sports events, along with a vibrant cultural procession.
 
• The Bundi Utsav is also famous for its **turban-tying competition** and bridal attire competition, which reflect the traditional Rajasthani lifestyle.
 
• Tourists and locals participate in the festival, making it a significant platform for promoting Rajasthan's art and culture on an international level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Madhya Pradesh**

 
 
• Madhya Pradesh is known as the "Heart of India" and is famous for its cultural heritage and historical landmarks.
 
• Popular festivals celebrated in Madhya Pradesh include **Khajuraho Dance Festival**, **Tansen Music Festival**, and **Malwa Utsav**.
 
• Khajuraho Dance Festival is a renowned classical dance event held annually near the Khajuraho temples.
 
 
 
• **Mizoram**
 
 
• Mizoram is a northeastern state of India, known for its scenic beauty and vibrant tribal culture.
 
• Popular festivals celebrated in Mizoram include **Chapchar Kut**, **Mim Kut**, and **Pawl Kut**, which are harvest festivals celebrated with traditional dance and music.
 
• Chapchar Kut is the most significant festival, marking the arrival of spring and celebrated with great enthusiasm.
 
 
 
• **Punjab**
 
 
• Punjab is famous for its rich cultural heritage, vibrant festivals, and traditional music and dance.
 
• Popular festivals celebrated in Punjab include **Lohri**, **Baisakhi**, and **Gurpurab**.
 
• Baisakhi marks the harvest season and is celebrated with joyous events like bhangra and giddha performances.

questions.question: In which of the following Indian states is the annual Hampi Dance Utsav celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hampi Dance Utsav, also known as the Hampi Utsav or the Vijaya Utsav, is an annual cultural festival celebrated in the state of **Karnataka**, India.
 
• It is organized in the town of Hampi, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and was once the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• The festival is a vibrant showcase of Karnataka’s rich cultural heritage through classical dance performances, music concerts, puppet shows, and other art forms.
 
• Hampi Utsav attracts thousands of visitors annually, including tourists and art enthusiasts, due to its unique cultural significance and the stunning backdrop of ancient ruins.
 
• This festival typically takes place in the month of November or early January and is organized by the Government of Karnataka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jharkhand**

 
 
• Jharkhand is a state known for its tribal culture, rich natural resources, and folk festivals such as Sarhul, Karma, and Sohrai.
 
• While Jharkhand hosts many traditional and tribal festivals, it is not associated with the Hampi Dance Utsav.
 
 
 
• **Odisha**
 
 
• Odisha is famous for its classical dance form, Odissi, and hosts various cultural festivals like the Konark Dance Festival and the Raja Parba.
 
• The Konark Dance Festival, held near the Sun Temple, is one of the most celebrated events in Odisha, but it is not related to Hampi Utsav.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu**
 
 
• Tamil Nadu is renowned for its Bharatanatyam dance form and festivals such as Pongal, Natyanjali Dance Festival, and Mamallapuram Dance Festival.
 
• Though Tamil Nadu is rich in cultural heritage, the Hampi Dance Utsav is not associated with this state.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hampi and its Significance**

 
 
• Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire during the 14th to 17th centuries and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The site is home to spectacular ruins, temples, and monuments, making it an iconic location for showcasing India’s cultural and artistic traditions.

questions.question: The Supreme Court Judges Removal motion must be signed by __________ members in the Lok Sabha or __________ members in the Rajya Sabha to adopt the motion in the parliament.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **1**__**00 members in the Lok Sabha and 50 members in the Rajya Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The motion for the removal of a Supreme Court Judge in India must be signed by** at least 100 members in the Lok Sabha** and **50 members in the Rajya Sabha** before being admitted.
 
• The process for the removal of Supreme Court Judges is outlined in **Article 124(4) of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The grounds for removal are limited to** proven misbehavior or incapacity**, ensuring that judges cannot be removed arbitrarily.
 
• Once the motion is admitted, it is referred to a three-member investigative committee comprising a Supreme Court judge, a Chief Justice of a High Court, and a distinguished jurist.
 
• If the committee finds the allegations valid, the motion needs to be passed by both Houses of Parliament with a **two-thirds majority of members present and voting** before the judge can be removed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968**

 
 
• The procedure for the removal of Supreme Court Judges is governed by the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.
 
• The Act elaborates on the process after the removal motion is admitted, including the formation of an investigative committee and voting thresholds in Parliament.
 
• The removal process ensures judicial independence by safeguarding against arbitrary dismissal.

questions.question: Which of the following water bodies typically has the highest salinity (dissolved salts)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ocean**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ocean water has the highest salinity** among natural water bodies, typically ranging from 34 to 36 parts per thousand (ppt), as it contains dissolved salts like sodium chloride, magnesium, and calcium.
 
• The salinity of oceans is primarily influenced by evaporation, precipitation, river inflow, and ocean currents. High evaporation rates in tropical regions result in higher salinity levels.
 
• **Dead Sea and certain areas of the Red Sea** are examples of regions with exceptionally high salinity due to minimal freshwater inflow and high evaporation rates.
 
• Marine organisms have adapted to high salinity levels, making oceans crucial for biodiversity and ecological balance.
 
• Oceans cover approximately 71% of Earth's surface and play a significant role in regulating the planet's climate and hydrological cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pond**

 
 
• Ponds are small, shallow freshwater bodies with low salinity levels as they primarily accumulate rainwater and runoff.
 
• They often support various aquatic plants and animals but are not significant contributors to global salinity levels.
 
• The salinity in ponds can increase due to pollution or lack of freshwater inflow but remains much lower than in oceans.
 
 
 
• **River**
 
 
• Rivers are freshwater systems with **negligible salinity** (typically less than 0.5 ppt), as they are primarily fed by precipitation, snowmelt, or springs.
 
• They transport dissolved minerals and salts to oceans, contributing to ocean salinity.
 
• Human activities like agriculture and industrial discharge can increase salinity levels in certain river systems.
 
 
 
• **Lake**
 
 
• Most lakes are freshwater bodies with **low salinity**, but saltwater lakes such as the Great Salt Lake or Lake Van can have high salinity due to evaporation and lack of outflow.
 
• The salinity levels in lakes vary based on geographical location, climate, and surrounding geological formations.

questions.question: Shruti Sadolikar is an Indian classical singer of the Khayal genre of which Gharana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shruti Sadolikar is a renowned Indian classical vocalist known for her contributions to the **Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana** of Hindustani classical music.
 
• The Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana is famous for its intricate and complex **ragas**, particularly rare or compound ragas like Basanti Kedar and Sampoorna Malkauns.
 
• Shruti Sadolikar trained under her father, Wamanrao Sadolikar, who was a disciple of Ustad Alladiya Khan, the founder of the Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana.
 
• She is celebrated for her deep understanding of rhythm (layakari) and her ability to present compositions with clarity and precision.
 
• In addition to her performances, she has played a pivotal role in preserving the traditions of the Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana and spreading awareness about its unique style.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Patiala Gharana**

 
 
• The Patiala Gharana is another prominent school of Hindustani classical music, known for its focus on **taans** (fast melodic passages) and **bol baant** (syllabic variations).
 
• This Gharana is associated with artists such as Bade Ghulam Ali Khan and his son Munawar Ali Khan.
 
• Unlike the Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana, the Patiala Gharana emphasizes emotional expression and ornamentation, making its style more accessible to audiences.
 
 
 
• **Rampur-Sahaswan Gharana**
 
 
• Founded in Uttar Pradesh, this Gharana is an offshoot of the Gwalior Gharana and emphasizes clear enunciation of lyrics and the beauty of the raga.
 
• Artists such as Ustad Nissar Hussain Khan and Ustad Rashid Khan belong to this school.
 
• This Gharana is known for its systematic raga development and intricate aakar taans.
 
 
 
• **Mewati Gharana**
 
 
• The Mewati Gharana is associated with the legendary Pandit Jasraj and is known for its devotional and spiritual approach to music.
 
• This Gharana focuses on the emotional rendering of ragas and often incorporates elements of **bhajans** and **kirtans**.
 
• It combines traditional techniques with modern sensibilities, making it highly popular among global audiences.

questions.question: Mudiyettu which was included in the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010, is a ritual dance drama of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mudiyettu** is a traditional ritual dance-drama performed in the state of **Kerala**.
 
• It is primarily associated with the worship of the goddess **Kali** and depicts the mythological tale of her victory over the demon **Darika**.
 
• Mudiyettu was inscribed on the **UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** in 2010, recognizing its cultural significance and traditional value.
 
• This art form is performed in temples and village shrines, serving as a communal celebration of good triumphing over evil.
 
• The performers use elaborate costumes, vibrant face paint, and traditional music to bring the characters and story to life, making it a visually captivating experience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odisha**

 
 
• Odisha is known for its traditional dance forms like **Odissi**, one of the classical dance styles of India, but it is not associated with Mudiyettu.
 
• Other notable folk traditions in Odisha include **Chhau dance** and **Pala** (a form of ballad singing).
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**
 
 
• Karnataka has its own rich heritage of traditional dance and theatrical forms, such as **Yakshagana**, a dance-drama performance combining music, dialogue, and elaborate costumes.
 
• However, Mudiyettu is not part of Karnataka's cultural repertoire.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu**
 
 
• Tamil Nadu is renowned for its classical dance form **Bharatanatyam** and folk traditions like **Karagattam** and **Therukoothu**.
 
• Although it shares cultural similarities with Kerala, Tamil Nadu does not practice Mudiyettu.

questions.question: Who was the last Mauryan king, killed by his Commander-in-Chief, leading to the establishment of the Shunga dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brihadratha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Brihadratha** was the last ruler of the Mauryan Empire, which was one of the most powerful empires in ancient Indian history.
 
• He was assassinated by his Commander-in-Chief, **Pushyamitra Shunga**, in 185 BCE during a military parade.
 
• This assassination marked the end of the Mauryan Empire and led to the establishment of the **Shunga dynasty**.
 
• The Shunga dynasty ruled parts of North and Central India and is known for its contributions to art and culture, particularly in promoting Buddhism and Hinduism.
 
• Brihadratha's reign is considered weak and marked the decline of the once-powerful Mauryan Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samprati**

 
 
• Samprati was a Mauryan ruler and the grandson of Emperor Ashoka.
 
• Known for his efforts in spreading Jainism, he is often compared to Ashoka for his religious contributions.
 
• He built numerous Jain temples and promoted the religion in the regions he ruled.
 
• Samprati's rule is remembered for its focus on religious tolerance and the propagation of Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Bindusara**
 
 
• Bindusara, the son of Chandragupta Maurya, was the second ruler of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He was known as "Amitraghata," meaning "Slayer of Enemies."
 
• Bindusara expanded the Mauryan Empire significantly, conquering several territories and ruling efficiently.
 
• He was the father of Emperor Ashoka, one of India's most famous rulers.
 
 
 
• **Dasharatha**
 
 
• Dasharatha was a Mauryan ruler and the grandson of Emperor Ashoka.
 
• He is believed to have succeeded Ashoka to the throne but was unable to maintain the empire's strength and unity.
 
• During his reign, there was a decline in the power and territory of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Dasharatha also played a role in continuing Ashoka's legacy of promoting Buddhism.

questions.question: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Amendment Act, 2024 establishes pollution control boards to prevent and control water pollution at _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the central and state level**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Amendment Act, 2024** focuses on the prevention, control, and abatement of water pollution in India.
 
• The Act establishes **pollution control boards at both the central and state levels** to oversee and regulate water pollution in their respective domains.
 
• The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** is responsible for laying down standards and coordinating the activities of state boards.
 
• The **State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)** implement the policies and standards set by the CPCB at the state level and ensure compliance with pollution control regulations.
 
• The Act empowers these boards to monitor water quality, issue directives to industries, and take necessary action against violators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Government Initiatives**

 
 
• Namami Gange Programme: Focuses on cleaning the Ganga River by reducing industrial and sewage pollution.
 
• Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM): Aims to provide safe, potable tap water to every rural household by 2024, including in areas with poor water quality.
 
• Jal Shakti Abhiyan: A campaign for water conservation and rainwater harvesting, focusing on groundwater recharge.
 
• National River Conservation Plan (NRCP): Broadens efforts to protect other rivers and water bodies from pollution.
 
• Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) & Smart Cities Mission: Address urban water supply and sanitation.
